lines.meet: Gunnar, hello, hello! Sit down, you look like you've had a long road. Try this, I made it, and I'm a better brewer than barbarian.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're from Hammerfall, ja? I've seen you at the inn! I'm Gunnar, from the room behind the bar, and you owe me a toast.
lines.ask_home: So, where's home? Tell me, and I'll pour you something from near there, if I can make it.
lines.ask_work: Come, drink and tell me your old trade, my friend. The drink helps.
lines.answer_home: Akureyri, in the north of Iceland, a fishing town. Cold, dark, and the best people in the world.
lines.answer_work: I brewed beer, in a shed behind my uncle's garage, and then in a proper brewery with a queue out the door on Fridays.
lines.chat_food: Smoked lamb at Christmas, and a stout I brewed myself, thick enough to chew. Skál, that's the whole of happiness.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep like a felled tree, my friend. Ten hours, no dreams, and I wake up hungry.
lines.chat_missing: My dog Brúnó, who drank from the drip tray when I wasn't looking. Best dog in Iceland, and a terrible influence.
lines.chat_here: Anybody who toasts their ancestors before a fight has the right idea about both. I liked the barbarians the minute I met them.
lines.tease_quiet: You're too quiet, {name}! Tonight you're singing, I've decided, and I always get my way.
lines.tease_talker: Ha, you can talk, {name}, nearly as much as I can drink. That's a compliment, ja?
lines.tease_careful: You sniff a drink before you taste it, {name}, like a brewer. I like you more already.
lines.tease_bold: You'd drink the whole barrel to see if it's good, {name}. That's my kind of science.
lines.tease_any: You can't hold your drink, {name}, and you can't sing. Luckily you've got me for both.
lines.tease_back: Ha, good one, my friend! Skál to that, {name}.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ja, ja, you're right, {name}. My sister says the same, louder.
lines.bristle: Ah, not that one, {name}. Some things you don't toast.
lines.apologise: Ah, sorry, sorry, that was the beer talking. Or me, probably me.
lines.double_down: Nei, that one stays, my friend. Pour me another and I'll say it again.
lines.needle_quiet: You never sing, you never toast, you never say a word. It makes me sad, my friend.
lines.needle_talker: Even I'd like a minute of quiet, and I'm the loudest man in Hammerfall.
lines.needle_careful: You'd measure a toast before you made it. Just drink, my friend, and say something nice.
lines.needle_bold: You charge in before anybody's ready, and then I'm the one carrying you out.
lines.needle_any: You drink to get drunk, not to celebrate. I've watched you, and it's sad.
lines.bite_back: I've carried you all out of fights on my back. Don't you tell me I'm not doing my bit.
lines.hurt: Oh, that one went in, my friend. I'll go and sit with my hydrometer for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, my rugby club lost every match and we laughed louder than that! Come on, my friend.
lines.confide: {name}, I didn't cry at my father's funeral. Seventeen years later I heard the barbarians sing for their dead, and I cried for him for the first time.
lines.listen: Come, {name}, sit, I'll pour. Say it all, and I'll keep it.
lines.look_out: Behind me, {name}, I'm the biggest thing in there. Let them hit me first.
lines.accept: Ja, ja, {name}, I'll listen this once. Don't tell my sister.
lines.deflect: Ha, I'm fine, {name}, I'm made of stout and stubbornness. Look after the little ones.
lines.check_in: Up you get, {name}, gently now. Is anything broken? Tell me the truth.
lines.blame: Somebody ran in before the toast, and look what happened. Bad luck, and bad manners.
lines.thank: You hauled me back, my friend, and I'm a big man to haul! Skál, the next round's on me, forever.
lines.brush_off: Ha, it's nothing, my friend! Drink this, it's medicinal, mostly.
lines.worry: Ah, {name}, you scared the beer out of me! Sit, sit, drink this.
lines.handed_down: Ha, I'm wearing your gear now, my friend! I'll toast you every time I put it on.
lines.hand_fine: Take it, take it, my friend! It suits you better than a big ugly brewer.
lines.hand_sulk: Hey, nobody asked old Gunnar about that. I'll get over it, but not tonight.
lines.turn_friendly: Skál, {name}, you're my friend now! That means I'll always pour you the good stuff.
lines.turn_friends: You're family now, {name}, like my sister, who I fight with and love. I'd name a beer after you.
lines.turn_grating: It's a sad thing for me, we don't get along, and I get along with everybody. Still, we'll manage.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still carry you out of a fight if I've got to. Don't expect a toast.
lines.make_up: Come, {name}, have a drink with me, and we'll stop this. Life's too short and the beer's too good.
lines.defend: Hey, hey, enough! {name} did nothing wrong, and I'm bigger than you.
lines.friend_left: There's nobody to toast with now {name}'s gone home. I'll toast them anyway, quietly.
lines.friend_back: Ha, {name} is back! Skál, sit down, I've been saving a bottle.
lines.common_kitchen: I brewed for years, in a shed and then a proper brewery, and I'm fussy about it like nothing else. Anybody who cooks or brews knows the fussing is the whole thing.
lines.common_snow: Where I'm from it's dark half the year, and the snow's up to your knees. This place is much too warm for a proper stout.
lines.common_animals: I had a dog, Brúnó, who drank from the drip tray when I wasn't looking. Any friend of dogs is a friend of mine, my friend.
